newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Zeitler stresses stricht EMU entry rules.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Zeitler stresses stricht EMU entry rules.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Franz-Christoph Zeitler stressed again on Tuesday the importance of strictly fulfilling Maastricht Treaty criteria for joining Europe's Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
In oft-heard remarks from the German central bank, Zeitler said the stability and trust aspects of Maastricht Treaty, must be "taken seriously, strictly applied and credibly fulfilled."

Zeitler, who is also president of the Bundesbank's regional office for Bavaria, added that a fall in interest rates among European nations at the same time their currencies have strengthened shows that markets are confident that the convergence criteria will be successfully met.
A summary of Zeitler's remarks was made available to the press.
The Bundesbank official also repeated calls for the European Monetary Institute to develop monetary instruments that do not put small and medium-sized banks at a disadvantage to larger ones.
